title: Each new foraminiferal chamber is a surface-tension figure; the whole shell is not

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Each new foraminiferal chamber is a surface-tension figure; the whole shell is not

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In multichambered organisms such as the foraminifera Globigerina or Rotalia, and in desmids, each newly formed bud or chamber is a figure of equilibrium shaped by surface tension while still fluid, and is then solidified onto earlier chambers, so the whole organism is not itself a figure of minimal area.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. V: The Forms of Cells

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The little organism as a whole is not a figure of equilibrium or of minimal area; but each new bud or separate chamber is such a figure, conditioned by the forces of surface tension, and superposed upon the complex aggregate of similar bubbles after these latter have become consolidated one by one into a rigid system.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter V, “The Forms of Cells”; topic “Forms fixed by successive solidification”. Scope: multichambered foraminifera, desmids and other organisms formed by successive stages of growth and consolidation

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch05-08: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.61

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The geometric prediction is quantifiable from 3D surfaces, and public specimens can test the chamber-versus-whole contrast. The causal role of surface tension during the unobserved fluid stage is harder to establish from finished shells.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reconstruct successive chamber surfaces in living or growth-staged foraminifera and test each new chamber against constant-mean-curvature or minimum-area surfaces under its boundary conditions, while testing the aggregate shell separately. Support requires good fits for new chambers but not for the whole shell and evidence of subsequent rigidification.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Desmid coverage is limited.

Boundary conditions and growth-stage timing are often unknown.

Rigid shells record final rather than fluid chamber geometry.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Endless Forams is large enough to fit chamber outlines of Globigerina-like tests and to ask whether the whole shell is a poorer minimal surface than its newest chamber. That is a real geometric test for planktonic foraminifera. It does not observe the fluid-then-solid sequence, and it omits desmids, so the mechanism and the full scope stay out of reach of this archive alone.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fit each foraminiferal chamber outline to a surface of constant mean curvature and fit the whole test to the same class of surface. Chambers that match and whole tests that do not would support the geometric claim; chambers that fit no better than the whole shell, or that fit a non-equilibrium family better, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The images are two-dimensional views of three-dimensional chambers.

A constant-mean-curvature outline does not show that the chamber was fluid when it formed.

Desmids and many benthic chambered forms are outside this image set.
